We just received a patent assertion from a third party alleging that a piece of model output (generated by Redwood-hosted inference used by one of our products) infringes their patent. I attached the notice (claim_notice.pdf) for your review.

James —

Thanks for flagging and for the notice. I'm looping in our legal (Kimberly) and ops (Monica, Aditya) so we can triage quickly. High level: we take third-party IP claims seriously and will start an internal triage. To be transparent, we may need to narrow the scope of what the MSA covers depending on whether the alleged infringement arises from (i) customer-provided content/prompts, (ii) Redwood model internal artifacts, or (iii) a customer integration we host.

Proposed first-step action items:
1) Immediate triage (48 hrs): our infra team will confirm whether the cited output was generated by your tenant and gather available metadata (model name, model version, timestamp ranges, request IDs).
2) Evidence exchange: please share a list of specific allegedly infringing outputs and the associated product flows. In return, we can provide a "forensic snapshot" limited to outputs, request metadata and cryptographic hashes (not raw training data). See the attached evidence checklist we normally use.
3) Legal exchange (5 business days target): Kimberly will propose redlines to the indemnity language (defend vs reimburse, settlement approval, scope). Please review the attached proposed_redlines_20271109.docx and let us know your hard constraints.
4) Escrow/insurance trigger: if the claim meets your threshold, we can discuss escrow or insurance coordination; please share insurer contact if you want a direct discussion.

Attachments: evidence_checklist.xlsx, proposed_redlines_20271109.docx (stubs)

We can also schedule a short triage call — I'm available today 2–4pm PT or Thursday morning.

-Ben

James / Ben —

I've reviewed the notice and Ben's proposed next steps. From Redwood legal's perspective, to accelerate resolution we suggest the following interim positions we can offer for negotiation:

1) Narrow scope: indemnity covers third-party claims arising solely from (a) Customer Content (as defined in the current MSA) and (b) direct outputs produced by the specific model version deployed to the customer's tenant. We will not accept open-ended indemnity for model architectures or upstream training artifacts.

2) Defense control: Redwood proposes the right to assume defense with counsel of our choice, subject to the customer's right to approve settlements that would (i) admit liability on the customer's behalf or (ii) impose non-monetary obligations.

3) Evidence production: Redwood will produce a limited forensic snapshot (request IDs, timestamps, model name/version, output text, and SHA256 hashes of outputs). We reserve the right to redact customer-submitted prompts where they contain customer confidential data — we will request those directly from NovaCorp.

4) Insurance and caps: indemnity obligations should be aligned with available insurance limits and the MSA cap. If NovaCorp requires escrow or alternative remedies, please provide insurer contact and an estimate of claimed damages for triage.

I've prepared a tracked-redlines document with proposed language (redlines_legal_track.docx attached). A few clarifying asks for NovaCorp legal:
- Please provide the full assertion (claims and accused products/code paths).
- Provide an initial estimate of damages and whether you're intending to trigger your insurance now.
- If you need a chain-of-custody forensic export, specify required fields and retention period.

We can commit to producing the limited forensic snapshot within 72 hours of agreement on scope and a narrow list of outputs to export.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Kim and Ben. Quick clarifications from NovaCorp's side:

- We understand the need to limit scope. Our core ask is that Redwood indemnify where the accused output was produced by Redwood's hosted model (i.e., not where the customer provided the infringing content). We can work with you on a narrowly tailored definition.

- Defense control: we prefer a joint defense model or, at minimum, that we are allowed to propose counsel and that settlements require mutual consent; we are uncomfortable with unilateral settlement control by Redwood.

- Forensics: we need chain-of-custody level details for the outputs you produce (timestamps, request IDs, signed hashes). We are prepared to share the exact example outputs that NovaCorp received. We need the initial snapshot within 72 hours given regulatory reporting timelines.

I've looped in our GC, Claire Mendoza, on this thread. She can coordinate on settlement approval thresholds and insurance.

Attached: claim_evidence_bundle.zip (contains claimant notice, example outputs)
